basics.name: Alexis Couvreur
basics.label: Co-founder at Reeveel · Software Engineer
basics.summary: I'm a software engineer based in Montreal, at home across the whole stack: frontend, backend, and the Linux underneath it all. I'm the technical lead on my teams, working closely with architects and leading the technical decisions. I maintain Sablier and contribute to TinyGo, Docker and a fair number of other Go projects. Open source is the part I care about most, inside companies as much as outside them.

work.name: Reeveel
work.summary: A startup building a new kind of digital frame for modern living spaces. I'm the CTO and I lead the engineering team.
highlights: Own the whole stack: firmware in C, a React Native app, Go APIs, a CLI and the SDKs
Built it local-first, so the frame works over Bluetooth with no account and no cloud
Set up the engineering side: infrastructure as code, CI/CD, signed and attested builds
Pushed the BLE fixes we needed back upstream to TinyGo and Espressif

work.name: Behaviour Interactive
work.summary: Built the public Creator Program page for Dead by Daylight, the studio's partnership program for streamers and video creators.
highlights: Shipped the whole page: creator benefits, program pillars, the Iridescent and Gold tiers with their eligibility rules, and the FAQ
Worked directly with the Dead by Daylight team on a two-month engagement

work.name: Banque Nationale du Canada
work.summary: I run the developer platform that thousands of engineers at the bank use every day: GitHub, Artifactory, and the golden path between them.
highlights: Technical lead on the platform team, working with the architects on standards and on where the platform goes next
Run GitHub and Artifactory for thousands of engineers, with every org, repo and permission declared in Terraform
Wrote the golden pipeline teams build on: build, test, publish, plus security gates, SBOM, provenance and signing
Kept the whole thing secretless. Artifactory and CI authenticate over OIDC, so there are no long-lived credentials to rotate
Wrote the Go tooling that provisions repos and reconciles drift against what Terraform declares
Started the bank's inner source community and still lead it: governance, coaching, onboarding
Sent our fixes to the GitHub Terraform provider upstream instead of keeping a fork

work.name: Supralog
work.summary: Lead developer on software for a national tournament federation, and the DevOps referent for the other teams.
highlights: Jenkins CI/CD with Kubernetes agents spun up on demand, and an on-prem cluster locked down with RBAC
Real-time monitoring with Telegraf, InfluxDB, Grafana, Prometheus and Alertmanager
Docker Swarm cluster with shared volumes and rolling updates, fronted by Traefik

work.name: Supralog
work.summary: Built the shared CI/CD platform that every engineering team ended up using.
highlights: Jenkins pipelines with platform-specific agents provisioned on demand from Kubernetes
Studied and benchmarked Google Cloud PaaS and IaaS (GKE) for the teams

work.name: I3S/CNRS
work.summary: Research on blockchain for IoT. Ran a private Ethereum network on Raspberry Pi and wrote Solidity contracts that handled sensor data and reconfigured actuators.

work.name: Ultra Prod SAS
work.summary: Designed, built and shipped VaiPharm, a cross-platform mobile app built with Apache Cordova.

projects.name: Sablier
projects.description: Scale-to-zero for containers: start workloads on demand, shut them down when activity stops. Works with Docker, Swarm, Kubernetes, Podman and Proxmox LXC.

projects.name: Traefik ModSecurity Plugin
projects.description: Traefik middleware that proxies requests through an OWASP ModSecurity Core Rule Set container, so you get a WAF in front of any Traefik-routed service.

talks.title: Comment générer des stubs WireMock avec OpenAPI Generator
talks.note: Lightning Présentations Éclairs, épisode 3, chez GoLogic
talks.description: A lightning talk on generating WireMock stubs straight from an OpenAPI spec, with a generator I wrote myself and got shipped in openapi-generator 7.3.0.

talks.title: Cloud Native Users and Contributor Stories
talks.note: Q2 meetup at the Google Montreal office
talks.description: One of the evening's lightning sessions, an end user story on building with and contributing to cloud native tooling.

talks.title: Sablier, scale to zero
talks.description: How Sablier starts containers on demand and shuts them down once nothing is using them, and how it slots in behind Nginx, Traefik and other reverse proxies.
